In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the LY-F core represents a sedimentological record of a large-scale continental landscape evolution, with a general northward shift of sedimentation areas from the late Carboniferous to the early Permian, and with a progressive increase of aridity.

the Carboniferous-Permian sedimentary record from the LY-F core, in the northern Massif central, is consistent with the palaeogeographic reconstruction proposed for the Massif Central and adjacent areas during the Late Paleozoic, i.e., a series of isolated basins separated by mountainous areas.

the Carboniferous to early Permian sedimentation in the northern Massif Centra was characterized by an overall progressive increase in the continental sedimentation, from the late Gzhelain to the late Sakmarain, which is consistent with an increasing aridification of the climate.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the LY-F core provides a reference for the Carboniferous and Permian stratigraphic succession of the northern Massifs Central, and that it can be used for the reconstruction of the palaeogeographic context in which these sediments were deposited.
the Carboniferous-Permian continental series of France, and probably also in the whole Variscan domain, is not a simple succession of sedimentary units deposited during a long-term subsidence phase.

the LY-F core is representative of the Carboniferous to Early Permian sedimentation in the northern Massif-Central, which is characterized by a progressive transition from lacustrine to playa-lake deposits, with a general trend towards shallowing.
